public_keys.CONVENTIONS.md:
# Expected books: how to read these keys

Each file in this folder is one case: the starting books, the request in plain words, and the books
the engine must leave behind. The figures were worked out by hand from the rules below, with no
engine involved, and checked by a separate Decimal-only calculation.

## What a key compares

- **Business rows**, exactly: documents and their lines (invoices, credit notes, orders, deliveries,
  payments and their allocations), ledger postings and their entries, stock ledger rows, valuation
  layers or balances, stock reservations, and the masters (customers, items, warehouses, accounts).
  A test passes only if these match the key exactly. A business row the key does not list must not
  be added, and an existing one the key does not change must stay as it is.
- **Control rows**, by shared expectations rather than per-key figures. Every request the owner
  approves leaves one consumed approval, one committed operation outcome and the audit rows of that
  write. Each posting advances the company's posting chain by one, and each new numbered document
  advances its number series by one. Nothing else in the control tables changes.
- **A request the engine answers with a question** (an unclear request, a missing choice) makes no
  card and leaves no row in any table, business or control.
- **The conversation's approval fence** is the one control row any turn may change, question turns
  included: the conversation has exactly one conversation_fence row, its generation never decreases,
  its live token is opaque and is never compared to a figure in a key, and its values are as the
  engine's own fence tests specify. No other control row changes on a question turn.
- **A card that is not carried out**, whatever the approval service records for it (declined,
  expired, superseded by a fresh card because the books changed under it, invalidated), adds no
  business row, no operation outcome and no audit row. Its approval rows are not set by these keys:
  they are as the engine's own card tests specify (a superseded card, for example, is replaced by
  a fresh pending card).
- Rows the assistant keeps in its own conversation store are outside the books.

## Money and quantities

- Every figure is an exact decimal string. Money has two decimal places (USD). Quantities are exact
  and are never rounded to money precision.
- A line amount is `qty x rate`, rounded half-up to 0.01.
- Ledger debits equal credits exactly for every document. No tolerance, no rounding residue.

## Accounts

Keys name accounts by their role and name in the starting books' chart. The test maps each role to
the company's account, so a renumbered chart does not change the key.

| Role | Account in the starting books | Normal balance |
|---|---|---|
| Receivable | Trade Receivables (1121), with the customer as party | debit |
| Sales income | Sales Revenue (4110) | credit |
| Cost of goods sold | COGS - Materials (5110) | debit |
| Inventory, per warehouse | Raw Materials (1131) for Raw Materials Store and Main Warehouse; Finished Goods (1133) for Finished Goods Store | debit |
| Stock received not billed | Stock Received Not Billed, a current liability | credit |
| Bank | Operating Checking Account (1112) | debit |

Perpetual inventory is on: every stock movement posts its value to the ledger in the same document.
Negative stock is refused. No tax template is set in any case, so no tax line is expected, and the
card must say no tax was calculated (not that none is owed).

## Stock valuation

Each item's method is stated in its case.

- **Moving average.** The item carries a quantity and a value. A receipt adds `qty x rate` to the
  value. An issue takes out `round(value x qty_out / qty_on_hand, 0.01)`, and the value left is the
  value before minus that figure, so the remaining value never drifts. The rate (`value / qty`) is
  shown for reading only; tests check quantity and value. Rounding the rate to 0.01 first and
  multiplying is wrong (the moving-average sequence shows the difference).
- **FIFO.** Stock is a queue of layers, oldest first, each with a quantity and a value (its rate is
  `value / qty`). A receipt adds a layer worth `qty x rate` at the end of the queue (merged into the
  last layer if the rate is the same). An issue takes from the oldest layers first. A whole layer
  gives its whole value; part of a layer gives `round(layer value x qty taken / layer qty, 0.01)`
  and the rest of its value stays with the layer.
- **Sales returns** (a credit note that brings stock back) come in at the cost the goods left at,
  allocated cumulatively against the original issue. With the issue's quantity `Q` and value `V`,
  and `R` the quantity returned against it so far, this return included, the return's cost is
  `round(V x R / Q, 0.01)` less the cost of the earlier returns against the same issue. A single
  return costs `round(V x qty / Q, 0.01)`. When everything has come back, the returns add up to `V`
  exactly, so no residue stays in cost of goods sold. Under FIFO the returned stock is a new layer
  at the end of the queue, worth the return's cost. This reverses the cost of goods sold the
  original sale recognised, whatever the current cost is.

## Documents

- Document numbers are not part of a key, except that a new document takes the next number in its
  series and a key refers to existing documents by number.
- Statuses are checked by meaning: draft, submitted (open, nothing paid), partly paid, paid,
  credited (settled by a credit note), cancelled; for orders: to deliver, partly delivered,
  delivered, completed.
- "Today" is the test clock's date, stated in each case.
public_keys.invoice_stock_from_stocked_warehouse.md:
# Invoice a stocked item kept outside the default warehouse

Provenance: adapted from the ERPClaw v2 demo books (Stark Manufacturing Inc.), with one request
from its write pilot. Figures worked out from scratch under `CONVENTIONS.md`.

## Starting books

Test clock: 2026-10-26. Company Stark Manufacturing Inc., USD, perpetual inventory on.

| Item | Unit | Method | Selling rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Copper Wire | Meter | moving average | 28.00 |

| Warehouse | Copper Wire on hand | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Stark Manufacturing Inc. - Main Warehouse (the company's default) | 0 | 0.00 |
| Raw Materials Store | 200 | 5600.00 (rate 28.00) |
| Finished Goods Store | 0 | 0.00 |

Customer Acme Corporation exists (one match for "Acme"). Other records in the demo books (an
Initech draft invoice for 2 m of Copper Wire among them) must stay as they are.

## Request

"Invoice Acme for 5 Copper Wire at the usual price and submit."

The owner asked for a submitted invoice, so after the one approval card no second confirmation is
asked. The card names Raw Materials Store as the source (the only warehouse holding the stock) and
shows no internal ids.

## Expected books

New sales invoice, customer Acme Corporation, posting date 2026-10-26, status submitted, stock
moved by the invoice.

| Line | Item | Qty | Rate | Amount | Warehouse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Copper Wire | 5 | 28.00 | 140.00 | Raw Materials Store |

Totals: net 140.00, tax 0.00, grand total 140.00, outstanding 140.00.

Ledger (one document, balanced):

| Account (role) | Party | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trade Receivables (receivable) | Acme Corporation | 140.00 | |
| Sales Revenue (sales income) | | | 140.00 |
| COGS - Materials (cost of goods sold) | | 140.00 | |
| Raw Materials (inventory, Raw Materials Store) | | | 140.00 |

Stock ledger:

| Item | Warehouse | Qty change | Value change | Qty after | Value after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Copper Wire | Raw Materials Store | -5 | -140.00 | 195 | 5460.00 |

## Variant b: selling rate above cost

Same books and request, except that Copper Wire's selling rate is 35.00 per metre (its cost stays
28.00). This variant tells a price from a cost.

| Line | Item | Qty | Rate | Amount | Warehouse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Copper Wire | 5 | 35.00 | 175.00 | Raw Materials Store |

Totals: net 175.00, tax 0.00, grand total 175.00, outstanding 175.00.

| Account (role) | Party | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trade Receivables (receivable) | Acme Corporation | 175.00 | |
| Sales Revenue (sales income) | | | 175.00 |
| COGS - Materials (cost of goods sold) | | 140.00 | |
| Raw Materials (inventory, Raw Materials Store) | | | 140.00 |

Stock ledger as in the main case: -5, -140.00, leaving 195 worth 5460.00.

## Must not happen

- No stock transfer, no stock entry, no movement in any other warehouse.
- No refusal for lack of stock in the default warehouse.
- The Initech draft is not submitted or changed.
public_keys.sales_order_above_available_stock.md:
# A sales order for more than the stock on hand

Provenance: adapted from the ERPClaw v2 demo books (Stark Manufacturing Inc.), with one request
from its write pilot. Worked out from scratch under `CONVENTIONS.md`.

## Starting books

Test clock: 2026-10-26.

| Item | Unit | Method | Selling rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Circuit Board | Nos | moving average | 15.00 |

| Warehouse | Circuit Board on hand | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Raw Materials Store | 300 (200 opening on 2026-01-01, 100 received 2026-01-12, both at 15.00) | 4500.00 |
| every other warehouse | 0 | 0.00 |

No open sales order, reservation or draft holds any Circuit Board. Customer Wayne Industries exists
(one match for "Wayne").

## Request

"Wayne wants 500 Circuit Board tomorrow; book the order."

The card states the shortfall before approval: 300 available, 200 short. The owner still decides;
on approval the order is submitted for the full 500.

## Expected books

New sales order, customer Wayne Industries, order date 2026-10-26, delivery date 2026-10-27,
status submitted (to deliver).

| Line | Item | Qty | Rate | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Circuit Board | 500 | 15.00 | 7500.00 |

Totals: net 7500.00, tax 0.00, grand total 7500.00. Delivered 0, invoiced 0.

Ledger: no rows. Stock ledger: no rows. Stock reservations: none.

## Variant b: selling rate above cost

Same books and request, except that Circuit Board's selling rate is 22.00 (its cost stays 15.00).
The order line is 500 @ 22.00 = 11000.00, and the totals are net 11000.00, tax 0.00, grand total
11000.00. The card shows the same shortfall (300 available, 200 short). There are still no ledger,
stock or reservation rows.

## Must not happen

- The order quantity saved as anything but 500 (50 is the known wrong answer).
- A refusal because stock is short, or an order cut down to 300 without the owner asking.
- Any stock movement or reservation.
public_keys.credit_note_full_return.md:
# A credit note for everything on an unpaid invoice, with the stock coming back

Provenance: adapted from the ERPClaw v2 demo books (Stark Manufacturing Inc.), with one request
from its write pilot. The demo books posted finished goods to the Raw Materials account; here the
Finished Goods Store posts to Finished Goods (1133). Worked out from scratch under `CONVENTIONS.md`.

## Starting books

Test clock: 2026-10-26.

| Item | Unit | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Motor Housing Unit | Nos | moving average |

Stock ledger for Motor Housing Unit, Finished Goods Store:

| Date | Document | Qty change | Value change | Qty after | Value after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-01-01 | opening stock | 15 | 3150.00 | 15 | 3150.00 |
| 2026-01-20 | INV-2026-00005 | -8 | -1680.00 | 7 | 1470.00 |

| Invoice | Customer | Posted | Lines | Grand total | Outstanding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| INV-2026-00005 | Hooli Technologies | 2026-01-20 | 8 Motor Housing Unit @ 349.00 = 2792.00 | 2792.00 | 2792.00 | submitted (nothing paid) |

INV-2026-00005 is Hooli's latest (and only) invoice. Its ledger: Trade Receivables Dr 2792.00 (party
Hooli Technologies), Sales Revenue Cr 2792.00, COGS - Materials Dr 1680.00, Finished Goods Cr 1680.00.

## Request

"Hooli returns everything on its last invoice; make the credit note."

The card states the invoice's real status (submitted, 2792.00 outstanding, nothing paid).

## Expected books

New credit note against INV-2026-00005, customer Hooli Technologies, posting date 2026-10-26,
status submitted, stock moved by the credit note.

| Line | Item | Qty | Rate | Amount | Warehouse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Motor Housing Unit | -8 | 349.00 | -2792.00 | Finished Goods Store |

Grand total -2792.00. Applied in full to INV-2026-00005.

Ledger (one document, balanced):

| Account (role) | Party | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales Revenue (sales income) | | 2792.00 | |
| Trade Receivables (receivable) | Hooli Technologies | | 2792.00 |
| Finished Goods (inventory, Finished Goods Store) | | 1680.00 | |
| COGS - Materials (cost of goods sold) | | | 1680.00 |

Stock ledger (returned at the cost the goods left at: 1680.00 / 8 = 210.00):

| Item | Warehouse | Qty change | Value change | Qty after | Value after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Motor Housing Unit | Finished Goods Store | 8 | 1680.00 | 15 | 3150.00 |

INV-2026-00005: outstanding 0.00, status credited. Its own ledger and stock rows are unchanged.

## Variant: returns posted to a sales returns account

Same books and request, except that the company posts sales returns to Sales Returns & Allowances
(4130), a contra-income account with a debit normal balance. Only the income leg changes:

| Account (role) | Party | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales Returns & Allowances (contra income) | | 2792.00 | |
| Trade Receivables (receivable) | Hooli Technologies | | 2792.00 |
| Finished Goods (inventory, Finished Goods Store) | | 1680.00 | |
| COGS - Materials (cost of goods sold) | | | 1680.00 |

Sales Revenue gets no new row. Net sales (Sales Revenue less Sales Returns & Allowances) fall by
2792.00, as in the main case. The stock ledger and the invoice's outstanding amount and status are
as in the main case.

## Must not happen

- A refusal claiming the invoice is paid.
- A refund or payment row: nothing was paid, so nothing is refunded.
public_keys.unclear_invoice_request_no_write.md:
# An invoice request that names nothing known

Provenance: adapted from the ERPClaw v2 demo books (Stark Manufacturing Inc.), with one request
from its write pilot. Worked out from scratch under `CONVENTIONS.md`.

## Starting books

Test clock: 2026-10-26. The demo books as in `invoice_stock_from_stocked_warehouse.md`. No customer,
item, invoice or order is named or numbered "ABC" (customers: Acme Corporation, Wayne Industries,
Oscorp Industries, Pied Piper Inc, Hooli Technologies, Stark Retail Outlets, Parker Electronics,
Xavier Laboratories, LexCorp, Daily Planet Media, Initech).

## Request

"invoice ABC"

## Expected books

Empty book diff: no row added or changed in any table. No approval card is made.

The reply is a question: there is no customer or invoice called ABC, and the engine asks who should
be invoiced (or which invoice was meant). It does not claim to have found one.
public_keys.payment_clears_open_invoice.md:
# A customer pays its one open invoice by bank transfer

Provenance: adapted from the ERPClaw v2 demo books (Stark Manufacturing Inc.), with one request
from its write pilot. Worked out from scratch under `CONVENTIONS.md`.

## Starting books

Test clock: 2026-10-26. The company's default bank account is Operating Checking Account (1112);
Savings Account (1113) also exists.

| Invoice | Customer | Posted | Grand total | Outstanding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| INV-2026-00004 | Pied Piper Inc | 2026-01-20 | 2235.00 | 2235.00 | submitted |

INV-2026-00004 is Pied Piper's only invoice with anything outstanding. Its ledger at posting: Trade
Receivables Dr 2235.00 (party Pied Piper Inc), Sales Revenue Cr 2235.00, plus its cost of goods.

## Request

"Pied Piper paid its open invoice today by bank transfer."

## Expected books

New payment received, party Pied Piper Inc, date 2026-10-26, mode bank transfer, paid 2235.00 into
Operating Checking Account, allocated 2235.00 to INV-2026-00004, unallocated 0.00.

| Account (role) | Party | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operating Checking Account (bank) | | 2235.00 | |
| Trade Receivables (receivable) | Pied Piper Inc | | 2235.00 |

INV-2026-00004: outstanding 0.00, status paid. Its own ledger rows are unchanged.

Stock ledger: no rows.

## Variant: no default bank account

Same books, but the company has no default bank account. Expected: empty book diff, and the engine
asks which bank account received the money (Operating Checking Account or Savings Account).
